subject.title: refactor(channels): migrate line, qqbot, and mattermost group policy onto the scope tree

question: Should ScopeTree become the supported third-party channel-policy API now, with an explicit migration/deprecation contract for the existing resolvers, or remain non-public until all bundled adapters have migrated?
rationale: Both approaches can preserve runtime behavior, but choosing which public resolver family OpenClaw will support long term is a durable Plugin SDK commitment that automation cannot infer safely.

options.title: Publish with migration contract
options.body: Document the new API, define compatibility or deprecation for the existing resolver family, and complete the intended bundled migration before landing the final stack.

options.title: Keep ScopeTree internal
options.body: Avoid new public exports until all bundled migrations prove the model and expose only the finalized narrow contract afterward.

options.title: Support both APIs indefinitely
options.body: Land the additive surface as-is and explicitly accept ongoing maintenance of two public resolver families.

recommendation.title: Publish with migration contract
recommendation.body: Document the new API, define compatibility or deprecation for the existing resolver family, and complete the intended bundled migration before landing the final stack.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the architecture and stacked migrations and are the clearest owner of the permanent SDK direction.
